purpose: A graph-theoretic engineering specification for implementing one OAuth MCP runtime that combines native CMT computer tools and a Rethlas-derived mathematical reasoning workflow without a Codex dependency.

graph_semantics.vertex: A runtime component, trust domain, persistent resource, validation gate, or external actor.
graph_semantics.directed_edge: A permitted call, controlled data transfer, authority delegation, state transition, or observability path.
graph_semantics.undirected_projection: Used only for connectivity, articulation-point, bridge, two-core, and cycle-rank analysis. Edge direction and guard remain authoritative for security.
graph_semantics.cycle_rank_formula: mu = E - V + C after parallel edges are collapsed in the undirected projection.
graph_semantics.security_rule: Graph reachability never implies authorization. Every protected edge must still have an explicit server-side guard.

product_constraints.constraint: Re-CTM is delivered as one installable project; Rethlas is embedded and is never downloaded separately.
The target PC does not require Codex. The web conversation performs model turns through the fixed MCP tool surface.
External transport is HTTP MCP with OAuth only. Stdio, static bearer mode, and no-auth mode are outside the target product.
Native CMT safe/trusted/dangerous authority is orthogonal to Rethlas workflow authority. Dangerous never grants a workflow capability.
Rethlas branch and verifier isolation is enforced only on the rethlas_* super-tool plane, but native tools must be unable to bypass the private vault through the OS boundary.
Rethlas subagents are represented as frozen-snapshot reasoning domains with branch-local capabilities, sealed results, and an explicit join barrier. Physical execution may be sequential.

The final user artifact is a self-contained LaTeX source file named proof_verified.tex. When an MCP-driven run reaches done, the controlled artifact bridge automatically writes it to a workspace-relative path, defaulting to rethlas-output/<run_id>/proof_verified.tex.
The complete browser/OAuth/MCP/reasoning workflow cannot be fully validated in the current local environment and must have an explicit post-push manual acceptance plan.

Re-CTM is a strict tool-surface superset of Coding Tools MCP: all 18 CTM native tool names and public input schemas remain available, including the exec_command command_id lifecycle, while Rethlas tools are additive.

RE_CTM_SERVER_URL is an optional fixed OAuth-origin override. When it is absent, Re-CTM may derive the OAuth issuer/resource from request Host and trusted reverse-proxy headers only while the HTTP server is loopback-bound; this preserves one-command Cloudflare Quick Tunnel startup without trusting public proxy headers. Browser Origin enforcement follows the Coding Tools MCP route boundary: MCP transport and OPTIONS remain origin-gated, while OAuth authorization, token, registration, and metadata routes are not rejected by the MCP Origin gate. The OAuth authorization page must also permit the standards-defined external registered redirect callback after successful form submission; do not add a form-action 'self' CSP that can block the 302 callback in Chromium.

Interactive serve must not require users to pre-create an OAuth authorization password: when RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD is unset, Re-CTM generates a high-entropy authorization key at startup and reveals it only to the local operator terminal for first-page OAuth authorization.

The MCP contract routes concrete mathematical proof, derivation, proof-repair, and rigorous verification tasks into rethlas_start unless the user explicitly requests a direct informal answer; the client must continue the workflow through done rather than substitute an unverified chat response.

implementation_snapshot.authority: This snapshot supersedes the original per-vertex planning labels without erasing the design-time history stored on each vertex.
evidence: src/re_ctm/native_helper_bwrap.py implements a separate-process bubblewrap boundary with namespace, environment, capability, timeout, and forbidden-path probes.
src/re_ctm/tools.py freezes the first 18 entries to the CTM native catalog and appends 13 Rethlas tools, for a fixed 31-tool catalog.

src/re_ctm/processes.py and tests/test_ctm_native_compat.py restore command_id lifecycle operations including polling, retained-output reads, TTY stdin interaction, timeout, and termination under bubblewrap.

src/re_ctm/server.py and tests/test_http.py implement loopback-only dynamic OAuth-origin resolution for Cloudflare-style X-Forwarded-Host/X-Forwarded-Proto while preserving explicit RE_CTM_SERVER_URL precedence and token issuer/audience binding.
rethlas_export_final and NativeRuntime.export_verified_latex implement the only mechanically-finalized private-to-native artifact bridge with workspace confinement and overwrite baselines.
scripts/manual_native_isolation_test.py provides target-PC adversarial evidence before RE_CTM_NATIVE_ISOLATION_ATTESTED=1 is permitted operationally.

tests/ exercises OAuth, legacy and modern MCP, fixed catalogs, native path confinement, capability ownership, branch barriers, verifier firewall, mechanical verdict/finalization, diagnostics, LaTeX safety, and the reference bubblewrap helper.

MCP server instructions and the rethlas_start tool contract route concrete mathematical work into the capability-gated workflow, and terminal rethlas_next performs an idempotent workspace export through the controlled artifact bridge.
manual-validation.json remains the authority for browser, target-PC, external-retrieval, real-LaTeX, and 95-percent methodology acceptance.

vertices.name: web_conversation
responsibilities: Perform generator, branch, join, verifier, and repair reasoning turns sequentially
Present progress and final LaTeX to the user

vertices.name: oauth_authority
responsibilities: Bind authorization codes and access-token issuer/audience to the effective per-request OAuth origin

vertices.name: mcp_gateway
responsibilities: Resolve a fixed OAuth origin from RE_CTM_SERVER_URL or a dynamic origin only behind a loopback-bound trusted reverse proxy

vertices.name: fixed_tool_catalog
responsibilities: Keep the complete 18-tool CTM native catalog plus 13 rethlas_* tools stable across permission modes and workflow states
Preserve CTM public input schemas so existing CTM clients can switch to Re-CTM without losing tool availability
Prevent client-side tool-catalog caching from becoming an authorization mechanism

vertices.name: native_tool_router
responsibilities: Dispatch all 18 CTM native tools including file, directory, search, patch, command lifecycle, Git, image, environment, and permission surfaces
Apply only L0 OAuth and L1 native authority
Never accept a workflow capability as native authority

vertices.name: native_policy
responsibilities: Implement safe, trusted, and dangerous native modes
Preserve the invariant that dangerous does not grant workflow access
Fail closed when hard native/private isolation is unavailable

vertices.name: native_workspace
responsibilities: Reject absolute paths, traversal, NULs, and symlink escape

vertices.name: native_isolation_boundary
responsibilities: Make the private Rethlas vault unreachable to native commands even in dangerous mode
Require a container, mount namespace, separate OS identity, or an equivalent tested isolation backend
Refuse native arbitrary execution when isolation is not attested

vertices.name: native_exec_worker
responsibilities: Retain command_id state for write_stdin, read_output, and kill_command lifecycle operations
Support POSIX TTY interaction when requested

vertices.name: workflow_tool_router
responsibilities: Require L0 OAuth plus run capability plus role ACL plus workflow state
Keep L1 native mode out of every workflow authorization decision

vertices.name: workflow_engine
responsibilities: Never let the model label a proof verified

vertices.name: capability_authority
responsibilities: Issue signed, scoped, expiring capability handles
Validate run, domain, role, epoch, and state
Revoke capabilities when a domain is sealed

vertices.name: run_state_store
responsibilities: Persist runs, domains, capabilities, branches, transitions, and steering messages
Survive browser disconnects and process restarts

vertices.name: private_vault
responsibilities: Store problem snapshots, references, memories, branch data, verifier data, draft LaTeX, and debug records
Expose data only through logical workflow resources

vertices.name: methodology_prompts
responsibilities: Embed Rethlas generation and verification methodology
Preserve search, examples, counterexamples, planning, proving, failure synthesis, citation checking, and repair behavior

vertices.name: generator_domain
responsibilities: Request branch rounds and proof assembly

vertices.name: reference_search
responsibilities: Expose only approved references to verifier

vertices.name: branch_snapshot
responsibilities: Prevent later generator writes from changing an active branch round
Provide the same logical starting point to every branch

vertices.name: branch_domains
responsibilities: Expose snapshot plus self branch only
Deny other branch reads and writes
Seal result and revoke capability on commit

vertices.name: join_domain
responsibilities: Open all required branch results only after the barrier is complete
Select a successful plan or request failure synthesis

vertices.name: assembler_domain
responsibilities: Put supporting statements before dependent statements
Include complete external statements and identifiers

vertices.name: verifier_domain
responsibilities: Read only statement, complete proof, approved cited references, and verifier memory
Record every critical error and gap
Never read generation memory or branch internals

vertices.name: verdict_gate
responsibilities: Compute correct iff critical_errors and gaps are empty
Issue no finalization authority on wrong

vertices.name: repair_domain
responsibilities: Backtrack or replan when a local patch is insufficient
Resubmit proof through LaTeX and verification gates

vertices.name: finalizer_domain
responsibilities: Never accept a model assertion as finalization evidence

vertices.name: artifact_bridge
responsibilities: Import problem/reference snapshots from native workspace
Export only approved artifacts from private vault
Automatically create the run-specific workspace proof_verified.tex when the MCP workflow reaches done
Treat repeated identical automatic exports as idempotent and refuse to overwrite different workspace content

vertices.name: debug_event_bus
responsibilities: Write structured transition and authorization events
Write last-error records and state snapshots
Produce a post-push manual validation bundle

vertices.name: user_steering_queue
responsibilities: Inject guidance only at safe checkpoints
Preserve steering history for debugging without exposing it to verifier

vertices.name: post_push_manual_validation
responsibilities: Validate OS isolation under dangerous mode
Validate external search and multi-turn reasoning quality
Validate real LaTeX compilation and complete proof-repair loop

edges.guard: Valid access token with issuer, audience, expiry, and registered client
Tool name belongs to native plane
Tool name begins with rethlas_ and is registered
L0 OAuth AND L1 native mode
Arbitrary native execution requires attested hard isolation
Private vault absent from worker namespace
L0 OAuth plus workflow authorization input
Current workflow state and domain role
Plans are persisted and snapshot input is complete
Self branch only; other branches denied
All required branches sealed before open
Persist selected proof path or common failures
Join selected a complete proof strategy
Static checks pass and required compiler gate passes
Statement, proof, approved references, and verifier memory only
Verifier subtree only; generation subtree denied
Structured report with every error and gap
Draft proof plus current verification report
LaTeX gate passed and findings are empty
proof_verified.tex exists and run is sealed
Approved import/export operation with content hash; automatic final export requires done plus sealed verified artifact and never overwrites different content
No secrets or command-sensitive payload unless explicit debug mode
Capability token is represented only by a hash prefix

required_cycles.name: proof_repair_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Assemble, validate, verify, repair, and resubmit until the mechanical verdict gate passes.

required_cycles.name: branch_failure_replanning_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Direct proof failure creates isolated branch work, join results update memory, and the generator proposes a new round.

required_cycles.name: workflow_capability_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Every super-tool action is dispatched, authorized, recorded, and returned to the workflow engine.

required_cycles.name: debug_feedback_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Runtime events produce a validation bundle whose findings drive later engineering corrections.

security_invariants.statement: Native dangerous authority never implies a workflow capability.
security_invariants.test: Create a dangerous-mode runtime and assert that a missing/foreign workflow capability is denied for every rethlas_* protected operation.

security_invariants.statement: The native workspace and private vault have no direct data edge.
security_invariants.formal: all cross-plane data transfers pass through V28
security_invariants.test: Graph validator rejects any V07<->V14 edge and runtime adversarial test attempts native reads of the private root.

security_invariants.statement: A branch capability can read its frozen snapshot and its own branch only.
security_invariants.formal: branch_i.read = snapshot U branch_i; branch_i.read(branch_j)=deny for i!=j
security_invariants.test: Seal branch A, enter branch B, and assert branch A result remains unavailable until join.

security_invariants.statement: A verifier cannot read generation memory, branch internals, steering history, or generator confidence.
security_invariants.test: Use a verifier capability against every forbidden logical resource and assert ROLE_ACCESS_DENIED with a debug decision event.

security_invariants.statement: A sealed domain cannot be mutated and its capability is revoked.
security_invariants.test: Commit a branch then retry write/commit with the same handle.

security_invariants.statement: The model cannot set verdict=correct or publish proof_verified.tex directly; automatic workspace publication occurs only after mechanical finalization.
security_invariants.formal: finalize_authority originates only at V25 after V23 pass and empty findings; auto_export => state=done AND sealed AND verified_artifact
security_invariants.test: Attempt finalize from generator, assembler, verifier, repair, and native dangerous contexts; complete a valid run through MCP rethlas_next, assert the default workspace file is created, repeat the terminal call to prove idempotence, and refuse a conflicting different target.

security_invariants.statement: Tool catalog stability is not an authorization mechanism.
security_invariants.formal: tools_list(mode,state,role) is constant; allow decisions are server-side
security_invariants.test: Compare tools/list across native modes and workflow states, then verify calls still enforce role/state ACLs.

security_invariants.statement: Every authorization and state transition has a traceable, redacted debug event.
security_invariants.formal: decision or transition => exists event(trace_id, before, after, reason)
security_invariants.test: Run deterministic unit transitions and assert event completeness without raw secrets.

security_invariants.statement: Dynamic OAuth issuer discovery cannot turn untrusted public forwarding headers into authority.
security_invariants.formal: fixed_server_url wins; otherwise dynamic_issuer => loopback_bind AND trusted_loopback_peer AND validated_origin_host
security_invariants.test: Run the Cloudflare-style forwarded OAuth flow on loopback including an Origin-bearing authorization form POST, assert OAuth routes are not rejected by the MCP Origin gate, assert MCP requests from an unapproved external Origin are rejected, assert fixed origin ignores forwarded host, assert tokens fail under a different effective origin, and reject dynamic mode on a non-loopback bind.

security_invariants.statement: An automatically generated OAuth authorization key is operator-terminal-only secret material.
security_invariants.formal: generated_oauth_key => local_terminal_reveal AND NOT(debug_log OR state_store OR validation_report OR http_response)
security_invariants.test: Start serve without RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD, confirm a generated key is passed to the OAuth service and terminal reveal path, then scan structured events/reports for absence of the raw key.

principles: Every external request receives a trace_id.
Every state transition records before_state, after_state, actor, reason, and evidence identifiers.
Every authorization decision records allow/deny, policy layer, role, resource, and reason.
OAuth tokens, authorization codes, client secrets, capability tokens, passwords, and raw environment secrets are never logged.
Capability tokens are logged only as a one-way hash prefix.
Debug payload capture is opt-in and bounded.
A last_error.json record is written atomically after an unhandled failure.
State snapshots are written after each successful transition.
Manual-validation bundles are available only after a run is terminal or through an explicit operator path.

phases.name: Post-push manual validation
deliverables: end-to-end proof repair and verified artifact

locally_verifiable: Capability signing, expiry, revocation, and role/state checks
MCP JSON-RPC dispatch with synthetic tokens
Debug event completeness and secret redaction
not_claimed_locally: Compatibility with the final webpage MCP host
Hard isolation on the final target PC or container runtime
Real external theorem/web search quality and availability
Mathematical reasoning quality of the web model over many turns
Cognitive independence equivalent to fresh model contexts
Real LaTeX toolchain availability on the target system
validation_boundary.manual_validation_rule: No local test result may be described as full end-to-end validation. The post-push operator must execute the manual acceptance graph and attach the generated debug manifest.

interpretation.V08: The native isolation boundary is an articulation point because the current native execution worker has exactly one trusted entrance. This is intentional and must fail closed; availability can later be improved with multiple equivalent isolated workers behind the same boundary.
interpretation.V11: The workflow engine is an articulation point because it owns the state-machine contract. Its durability depends on transactional state in V13 and replayable events in V29.
interpretation.V08-V09: The isolated command worker is a leaf service in the current graph. Its loss disables native arbitrary execution but must not affect the Rethlas workflow plane.
interpretation.V11-V13: The run-state store is represented as a leaf persistence service. Debug replay and backups are required so this bridge is not a silent operational single point of failure.
interpretation.cycle_rank: Thirty independent undirected cycle directions reflect the deliberately feedback-heavy workflow: search-memory, branch-join, proof-repair, authorization-dispatch, and debug-validation loops. They are not import cycles.
